verses.117:3: Diga agora a casa de Aarão: * {quoniam_dicat} {misericordia}.
verses.117:4: Digam agora os que temem o Senhor: * {quoniam_dicat} {misericordia}.
verses.117:5: Da tribulação invoquei o Senhor: * e o Senhor me escutou {latitudine}.
verses.117:6: {adjutor}: * não temerei o que me faça o homem.
verses.117:8: {bonum} confiar no Senhor, * {quam} confiar no homem:
verses.117:12: Cercaram-me como abelhas, † e se inflamaram como fogo em espinhos: * {ultus}.
verses.117:15: Voz de exultação e de salvação * nas tendas dos justos.
verses.117:16: {Dextera} do Senhor {fecitvirtutem}: † {dextera} do Senhor me exaltou, * {dextera} do Senhor {fecitvirtutem}.
verses.117:17: Não morrerei, mas viverei: * e narrarei as obras do Senhor.
verses.117:18: {castigans}: * e à morte não me entregou.
verses.117:19: {aperite} as portas da justiça, † {ingressus}, {confitebor_domino}: * esta é a porta do Senhor, os justos entrarão por ela.
verses.117:22: A pedra que os construtores rejeitaram: * {caputanguli}.
verses.117:23: {adomino}: * e é maravilhoso aos nossos olhos.
verses.117:25: Ó Senhor, salvai-me, † ó Senhor, {prosperare}: * bendito o que vem {innomine}.
verses.117:26b: {benediximus} da casa do Senhor: * {deusdominus}, e brilhou para nós.
verses.117:27b: Estabelecei um dia solene {condensis}, * até {cornu} do altar.

decisions.latin: Confitémini Dómino … confitébor Dómino … Confitébor tibi … et confitébor tibi
decisions.why: confitéri to God (ἐξομολογεῖσθαι) was open in the glossary when this psalm was drafted, with 'louvar' pencilled in; when I re-read glossary.md before draft 2 the row stood as 'dar graças a', status settled (D5), which is the verb used here from draft 1. It frames this psalm (117:1 = 117:29) and returns four times inside it, so one decision fills every occurrence and the verb can be switched through the whole psalm at once. Ps 53 (53:8 confitébor nómini tuo), finished tonight, proposes 'dar graças', on two facts checked in the DO Latin psalter: confitéri stands in one verse with laudáre as its parallel (34:18, 108:30), so 'louvar' for both would make one word of two; and 'grátias ágere' never occurs in the psalms, so 'dar graças' is free. This psalm adds two more: laus stands in 117:14 (laus mea Dóminus → o meu louvor), and in 117:28a 'louvarei' would rhyme with 'exaltarei' at mediant and final, where the Latin has no echo (tibi / te).

options.label: dar graças
options.note: Draft: the verb Ps 53 proposes, kept the same. It keeps the Latin dative (Dómino → ao Senhor), fits a psalm that gives thanks for a rescue (quóniam exaudísti me), leaves 'louvar / louvor' to laudáre / laus, and is safe under rule 3 (Dai / dei). The incipit comes out word for word as the Diurnal Monástico 1962 prints it beside this Latin ('Dai graças ao Senhor, porque êle é bom'). Cost: the root of confession — acknowledging aloud — is heard only faintly.

options.label: louvar
options.note: The glossary's pencilled word; Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT throughout this psalm, Douay-Rheims 'give praise'. Plain and beloved; collides with laudáre, puts 'louvarei' beside 'o meu louvor' of 117:14 where the Latin has two roots, and makes 117:28a rhyme (louvarei / exaltarei).

options.label: confessar
options.note: The cognate. 'Confessai ao Senhor' is heard as a call to confess sins, which the glossary keeps for 31:5, and 'Eu vos confessarei' as 'I will hear your confession'.

decisions.why: The refrain of this psalm (117:1–4, 117:29), of Pss 105 and 106, and — with in ætérnum — of all 27 verses of Ps 135. The glossary's working form is 'porque para sempre é a sua misericórdia'. Here it is said four times running by alternating choirs, which is the test the brief asked for. Said aloud four times, the working form trips twice: 'porque para' opens on a stutter of p-r syllables (por-que-pa-ra), and 'sempre é a sua' piles three vowels in hiatus (-e é a). The slot holds the refrain without its conjunction, so that the question of 117:2–4 (decision 'dicat') can be answered separately and the refrain still cannot drift.

options.label: porque é para sempre a sua misericórdia

forms.misericordia: é para sempre a sua misericórdia

options.note: Draft, and a proposal for the glossary. Same words as the working form, the copula moved up: 'porque‿é' and 'sempre‿a' each make one clean elision, 'para sempre' still stands before the subject as in sǽculum does, and the line still closes on 'misericórdia' as the Latin closes on misericórdia ejus (paroxytone cadence, 14–15 syllables for the Latin's 15). It gives Ps 135 a twin of the same build (porque é … a sua misericórdia).

options.label: porque para sempre é a sua misericórdia

forms.misericordia: para sempre é a sua misericórdia

options.note: The glossary's working form. The Latin's order exactly; heavier in the mouth for the two reasons given above, and it is said five times here and twenty-seven times in Ps 135.

options.label: porque a sua misericórdia é para sempre

forms.misericordia: a sua misericórdia é para sempre

options.note: The order of plain speech, and of Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT ('a sua misericórdia é eterna'). Closes firmly on 'sempre'; but the refrain then ends on the adverb, not on the mercy, and under the tone the final cadence falls on 'para sempre' five times.

options.label: porque eterna é a sua misericórdia
options.note: Offered only so that it can be weighed: I believe this is close to the refrain as it is sung at Mass in Brazil, but that is from memory and UNVERIFIED — nothing in the parallels file has it (Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT: 'a sua misericórdia é eterna'; the Diurnal, from the Hebrew: 'eterno é o seu amor'). Refused as the text: the glossary keeps in sǽculum → para sempre apart from in ætérnum → eternamente on purpose, and this would merge them.

decisions.latin: Dicat nunc Israël quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum…
decisions.why: After dícere, quóniam is the Vulgate's calque of ὅτι and can be 'that' (Douay-Rheims 'Let Israel now say that he is good: that his mercy…'; Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT 'que') or the first word of the thing said — the people are told to say the refrain itself, conjunction included. The Hebrew explains the Latin here: there the quoted words are the refrain with its ki. In 117:3–4 the Latin's own colon and asterisk set the refrain off as the thing said. Portuguese must choose between 'que' and 'porque'; the Latin column prints the identical five words in 117:1–4 and 117:29.

options.label: Diga agora Israel: porque ele é bom, * porque…

forms.v2a: Diga agora Israel: porque ele é bom,

options.note: Draft. The refrain is word for word the same in all five verses, as in the Latin (rule 6), and each group answers with the acclamation of 117:1. The Diurnal Monástico 1962 also prints it as quoted speech ('Que ela o diga, a casa de Israel: * eterno é o seu amor!'). A colon is put after 'Israel' to mark the quotation; the Latin's colon before the asterisk becomes a comma in this one verse.

options.label: Diga agora Israel que ele é bom: * que…

forms.v2a: Diga agora Israel que ele é bom:

options.note: Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT: quóniam as 'that'. Smooth, and the commoner reading of dícere quóniam; the refrain then begins with 'que' in three verses and 'porque' in two, where the Latin has one word.

decisions.why: A pregnant Septuagintal phrase (ἐπήκουσέν μου εἰς πλατυσμόν): heard me 'in / into breadth' — the wide place set against tribulátio, the tight one. Ps 4:2a has the same pair as a verb (in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi → 'me abristes espaço' in Ps 4 draft 2). Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 both supply a second verb ('and enlarged me', 'e pôs-me ao largo'); the Latin has only the noun. latitúdo recurs: 17:20 edúxit me in latitúdinem, 118:45 ambulábam in latitúdine; 30:9 has the other phrase, in loco spatióso.

options.label: na amplidão
options.note: Draft 2, from the stylist. A noun for the noun, nothing supplied, and only spatial: wide open space, which is what latitúdo is against the tightness of tribulátio. It can serve the other places unchanged (17:20 'para a amplidão', 118:45 'andava na amplidão'). Colon 3 syllables short of the Latin.

options.label: na largueza
options.note: Draft 1. The nearest noun to latitúdo; but both blind readers heard open-handedness before breadth — the stylist said so, the ambiguity reader's likeliest hearing was 'heard me generously', and it listed the word as unknown.

options.label: em lugar espaçoso
options.note: Clear and concrete, and the Latin's length exactly; supplies 'lugar', and is word for word what 30:9 in loco spatióso will want.

options.label: e me pôs ao largo
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Supplies a verb; and in Brazil 'ao largo' is first 'at a distance, offshore'.

options.label: e me abriu espaço
options.note: Ties the verse to Ps 4:2a ('me abristes espaço'); supplies a verb, as Douay-Rheims does ('and enlarged me').

decisions.why: The same half-verse opens 117:6 and 117:7, so one slot. adjútor (βοηθός) is the agent noun beside adjutórium → auxílio (Ps 90) and adjuváre → auxiliar (Ps 53's proposal); it is all over the psalter. The Latin has a dative and no verb ('the Lord [is] to me a helper'). Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT have 'o meu amparo', which the glossary now keeps for suscéptor.

options.label: O Senhor é o meu auxílio

forms.adjutor: O Senhor é o meu auxílio

options.note: Draft. The glossary's family (auxílio / auxiliar); the copula supplied and the dative turned into a possessive, as Matos Soares does. Cost: adjútor and adjutórium become one word, as suscéptor → amparo also turns an agent into an abstract noun.

options.label: O Senhor é para mim auxílio

forms.adjutor: O Senhor é para mim auxílio

options.note: Keeps the dative, and matches 'se fez para mim salvação' (factus est mihi in salútem) further on; a little stiff.

options.label: O Senhor é o meu auxiliador

forms.adjutor: O Senhor é o meu auxiliador

options.note: The Latinist's fix (minor, on both verses): adjútor names the one who helps, and 'auxílio' reaches him only by metonymy. He is right about the noun, and the word stays in the glossary's family. Refused as the text: it makes the half-verse 11 syllables for the Latin's 8, twice running; 'auxiliador' is hardly said in Brazil outside the Marian title; and the same metonymy is already the glossary's way with suscéptor → amparo and Matos Soares' way here ('o meu amparo'). If agent nouns are to be kept as agents across the psalter, this is the form.

options.label: O Senhor é quem me ajuda

forms.adjutor: O Senhor é quem me ajuda

options.note: Keeps the agent (Douay-Rheims 'my helper') with the plainest verb; splits the family auxílio / ajudar.

decisions.why: despícere is 'to look down upon' and by figure 'to despise' (L&S); the LXX has ἐπόψομαι, 'I shall look upon', Douay-Rheims 'I will look over my enemies'. Ps 53:9 (super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus), finished tonight, chose 'olhar de cima' because Portuguese has the same double sense in that one idiom, and named this verse as the next place for it.

options.label: olharei de cima
options.note: Draft, following Ps 53. The literal picture with the contempt inside it.

options.label: desprezarei
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Only the figurative half; the Greek behind the Latin is a verb of seeing.

decisions.latin: Bonum est confídere in Dómino, * quam confídere in hómine
decisions.why: A Hebraism through the Greek (ἀγαθὸν … ἤ): the positive 'bonum' with 'quam' does the work of a comparative. Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT write 'É melhor … que'; Douay-Rheims keeps 'It is good … rather than'. bonum also answers 'quóniam bonus' of the refrain. The two verses are one frame said twice, with confídere (πεποιθέναι) in the first and speráre (ἐλπίζειν) in the second: confiar / esperar, kept distinct (Matos Soares and the Diurnal blur them).

options.label: É melhor … do que
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. The degree of the adjective is grammar, and yields (rule 2); 'melhor' is still bonum.

options.label: É bom … mais que
options.note: Keeps the positive, and with it the echo of 'porque ele é bom'; sayable, slightly foreign, exactly as foreign as the Latin.

decisions.why: The stylist's cadence remark: 'príncipes' is proparoxytone and leaves two syllables after the last accent.

options.label: esperar nos príncipes
options.note: Draft, kept. The same build as 117:8 ('confiar no homem'), so the two verses stay one frame said twice; and the Latin verse closes on the same proparoxytone (princípibus).

options.label: nos príncipes esperar
options.note: Stylist: closes on the repeated verb, oxytone. Refused as the text: an inversion nobody would say (rule 5), and it breaks the parallel with 117:8.

decisions.latin: et in nómine Dómini quia ultus sum in eos
decisions.why: The second refrain, three times running; one slot. The Latin is abrupt: 'and in the name of the Lord — quia — I took vengeance on them'. The quia mirrors the Hebrew ki and is not in Rahlfs' Greek; Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT all leave it out. ultus sum is the deponent perfect of ulcísci.

options.label: e foi em nome do Senhor que me vinguei deles
options.note: Draft. A cleft sentence: the copula is supplied (rule 2 allows it) and quia becomes the 'que' that the cleft needs, so every Latin word is heard, in the Latin's order, and the weight falls on the name as it does in the Latin. 14 syllables for the Latin's 16.

options.label: e em nome do Senhor me vinguei deles
options.note: Douay-Rheims and pt-PT: quia left out. Shorter (12).

options.label: mas eu tomei vingança deles em nome do Senhor
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Natural order; 'et' becomes 'mas', and the name loses the first place.

decisions.why: The Latin has the masculine eos although its antecedent in 117:10 is the feminine gentes — agreement by sense (the men). Portuguese 'nações' is feminine too, so the same choice arises; Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT write 'delas' in all three verses.

options.label: deles
options.note: Draft, kept: the Latin's own gender. In 117:12 it matters to the ear: after 'Cercaram-me como abelhas', 'me vinguei delas' can be heard as vengeance on the bees. The ambiguity reader understood 'deles' as 'the people of the nations that surrounded him' — the Latin's agreement by sense exactly — while noting that the step from 'nações' to 'deles' may cause a moment's hesitation.

options.label: delas
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT, and the stylist's remark on 117:10 and 117:12: the ear looks for a masculine antecedent and has heard 'as nações'. Refused as the text because the hesitation is the Latin's own (gentes … eos) and because of the bees; it is one slot, so it can be switched in all three verses at once.

decisions.why: The same three words four times: in the vengeance refrain and in 'benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini'. One slot, so that they stay identical. Ps 53:3 (in nómine tuo) chose 'no vosso nome', keeping the article before the possessive; here there is no possessive, and the fixed locution is free.

options.label: em nome do Senhor
options.note: Draft. For 117:26a it is what all three Portuguese antecedents in the parallels file print ('Bendito o que vem em nome do Senhor': Matos Soares 1932, Diurnal Monástico 1962, pt-PT), and Matos Soares and the Diurnal have it in 117:10–12 as well.

options.label: no nome do Senhor
options.note: pt-PT in 117:10–12 (but not in 117:26a). Matches Ps 53's 'no vosso nome' and keeps 'in' as open as the Latin between 'in' and 'by'; it would make 'bendito o que vem no nome do Senhor', against the wording everyone knows.

decisions.latin: Circumdántes circumdedérunt me … Castígans castigávit me Dóminus
decisions.why: Twice the psalm has the Hebrew infinitive absolute as the Greek and Latin give it: participle + finite verb of the same root (κυκλώσαντες ἐκύκλωσαν, παιδεύων ἐπαίδευσεν). Rule 2 forbids dropping a repetition the Latin has; Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT drop both ('Pondo-se à roda de mim', 'severamente'). One decision, so that the figure is treated the same way in both verses.

options.label: gerund + verb
options.note: Draft. The Latin's own figure, root said twice (Douay-Rheims 'Surrounding me they compassed me about', 'The Lord chastising hath chastised me'). circumdáre → cercar (glossary). Draft 2 names the subject in 117:11 ('eles'), from the stylist: draft 1's 'Cercando-me, me cercaram' put two 'me' side by side and the mouth tripped; he said of his own accord that the repetition of 'cercar' belongs to the text. The colon now has the Latin's ten syllables.

options.label: verb said twice
options.note: The diction of the Diurnal Monástico 1962, which doubles the finite verb ('castigou-me, castigou-me de nôvo', 'Empurraram-me, empurraram-me'). More like speech; the participle is gone and 'sim' is supplied.

options.label: adverb

forms.circumdantes: Pondo-se à minha volta, me cercaram

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 / pt-PT. Explains the figure instead of giving it; the repetition is lost.

decisions.why: Two passives and a purpose clause: 'pushed, I was overturned so that I should fall' (ὠσθεὶς ἀνετράπην τοῦ πεσεῖν; Douay-Rheims 'Being pushed I was overturned that I might fall'). evértere is 'to overturn, upset, throw down' (L&S). The Latin is odd in the same way as any close rendering: the man is already overturned, and yet the falling is still a purpose, and the Lord catches him. Matos Soares 1932 softens it into an attempt ('Procuraram derribar-me … estive quase a cair').

options.label: Empurrado, fui derrubado para cair
options.note: Draft. Both passives and the purpose kept, in the Latin's order.

options.label: Empurrado, fui abalado para que caísse

forms.eversus: Empurrado, fui abalado para que caísse

options.note: Removes the oddity (shaken, not yet down); weaker than evértere.

options.label: Empurraram-me para cair
options.note: pt-PT: one verb for two, and an active for the passives.

decisions.why: suscípere (ἀντελάβετο) is the verb of suscéptor, which the glossary renders 'amparo' (open, Ps 90:2). The verb and the noun should go together.

options.label: me amparou
options.note: Draft: the verb of 'amparo'; to catch and hold up someone who is falling is exactly what 'amparar' says.

options.label: me susteve
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Good, a little bookish in Brazil; cuts the tie with suscéptor.

decisions.why: fortitúdo (ἰσχύς) must stay apart from virtus, which comes two verses later and for which Ps 53 proposes 'poder' (the two stand together in 67:36 virtútem et fortitúdinem). The same line stands word for word in two canticles of the DO psalter folder (ids 15:2 and 12:3 there), so it wants one rendering.

options.label: a minha força
options.note: Draft. The plain word, left free by virtus → poder.

options.label: a minha fortaleza
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT; the cognate, and the name of the virtue. In Brazil it is first a fortress, which the Latin word is not.

decisions.latin: Fortitúdo mea, et laus mea Dóminus
decisions.why: The Latin puts the two predicates first and the Lord last, with no verb. The stylist heard draft 1's 'A minha força e o meu louvor é o Senhor' as asking for 'são' until 'o Senhor' arrives — a parse the reciter has to revise in mid-colon.

options.label: O Senhor é a minha força e o meu louvor

forms.v14a: O Senhor é {fortitudo} e o meu louvor

options.note: Draft 2, from the stylist; it is also the order of Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and Douay-Rheims ('The Lord is my strength and my praise'). Order is what rule 2 gives to the ear; every word is kept.

options.label: A minha força e o meu louvor é o Senhor

forms.v14a: {fortitudo_cap} e o meu louvor é o Senhor

options.note: Draft 1. The Latin's order, closing on 'Senhor' as the Latin closes on Dóminus; the singular verb after two subjects-to-the-ear is the stumble.

decisions.latin: et factus est mihi in salútem … et factus es mihi in salútem
decisions.why: A formula said three times here (once of God, twice to him) and again in the two canticles that share 117:14. 'in salútem' is a Hebraism through the Greek (ἐγένετό μοι εἰς σωτηρίαν: 'became to me for salvation'). The psalm also runs on the verb fácere — fecit virtútem, factus est, factum est istud, quam fecit Dóminus — which 'tornar-se' would interrupt. salus → salvação (glossary).

options.label: e se fez salvação para mim

forms.factusest: e se fez salvação para mim
forms.factuses: e vos fizestes salvação para mim

options.note: Draft 2. fíeri → fazer-se (as in 'se fez carne'), the dative kept (mihi → para mim), 'in' left to grammar. The order is the stylist's, taken in all three verses: in draft 1 'para mim' stood between the verb and 'salvação' and he heard the phrase as mounted on the Latin (117:14, 117:21, 117:28b). His verb ('tornou') is not taken — see the third option.

options.label: e se fez para mim salvação

forms.factusest: e se fez para mim salvação
forms.factuses: e vos fizestes para mim salvação

options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's order (mihi in salútem).

options.label: e se tornou salvação para mim

forms.factusest: e se tornou salvação para mim
forms.factuses: e vos tornastes salvação para mim

options.note: The stylist's line as given. Refused as the text only for the verb: the psalm runs on fácere (fecit virtútem, factus est, factum est istud, quam fecit Dóminus) and 'fazer-se' carries that thread at no cost to the ear.

options.label: e se tornou a minha salvação

forms.factusest: e se tornou a minha salvação
forms.factuses: e vos tornastes a minha salvação

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT (Douay-Rheims 'is become my salvation'). The most natural; the dative becomes a possessive and the thread of fácere is cut.

decisions.why: Said three times in one verse. Ps 90:7 already has 'à tua direita' for a dextris tuis.

options.label: A direita
options.note: Draft, with the Diurnal Monástico 1962. The current word.

options.label: A destra
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT ('dextra'; the Diurnal has 'destra' once too). Shorter and hieratic; a word met only in church.

decisions.why: fácere virtútem (ἐποίησεν δύναμιν; Douay-Rheims 'hath wrought strength') is a Hebraism, said twice here round 'exaltávit me', and again in 59:14 = 107:14 (In Deo faciémus virtútem). Ps 53 proposes virtus → poder. Portuguese cannot say 'fez poder': either the light verb yields or the heavy noun does.

options.label: agiu com poder
options.note: Draft. Keeps the glossary-grade noun (poder) and lets 'fazer' go; serves 59:14 too ('Em Deus agiremos com poder').

options.label: mostrou o seu poder
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Adds 'seu' and turns doing into showing.

options.label: fez proezas
options.note: Keeps 'fazer', and 'proeza' is virtus as a deed of valour; but a plural for a singular, and it leaves the glossary's word for virtus.

options.label: fez maravilhas
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico 1962. Sings well; it is the word mirabília will need.

decisions.why: Rule 3: the vós imperative of abrir is 'abri', which is also 'I opened' — the glossary lists it by name as a form to avoid. Every Portuguese antecedent has 'Abri-me as portas da justiça'. The verb must be recast or replaced. The only other Aperíte in the DO psalter folder is a canticle (id 26:2, Aperíte portas), which will need the same ruling. Ruled (D13): the ban on -ir imperatives is a ban on the bare form, which the ear can take for “I opened”. With the enclitic (Abri-me as portas) the first-person reading would need a reflexive nobody hears; Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 both have exactly this; and the Latinist marked the loss of the imperative “major” on both drafts. So the imperative returns, and the gate is clean on this verse.

options.label: Abri-me
options.note: Draft 3, ruled by the main session (DECISIONS.md D13). Matos Soares 1932, Diurnal Monástico 1962, pt-PT. Both blind readers asked for the imperative, neither knowing rule 3: the Latinist marked the jussive 'major' (Aperíte is an active second-person plural; the passive removes the people addressed) and the stylist found it ceremonious; both wrote 'Abri para mim'. Against rule 3 as written ('abri' is named in the glossary), and rule 3 is Gustavo's decision, so it is not the text. In its favour: with '-me as portas' after it the first-person reading ('I opened the gates for myself') is far-fetched, where 'Abri para mim' would leave it open. If Gustavo allows the exception, this is the text — and the Latinist gate is not clean on this word until he rules.

options.label: Abram-se para mim
options.note: Draft 2’s wording. Draft. The verb 'abrir' and the dative kept (mihi → para mim); the imperative to unnamed gatekeepers becomes a jussive. Nobody is addressed in the Latin by name either.

options.label: Descerrai-me
options.note: A true imperative and no homograph; a word from inaugurations, not from speech.

decisions.why: ingréssus is a perfect participle: the entering comes before the thanksgiving.

options.label: tendo entrado por elas
options.note: Draft 2, the Latinist's fix (taken): the plain gerund did not keep the priority clearly. Two syllables over the Latin.

options.label: entrando por elas
options.note: Draft 1. Lighter, and a gerund before the main verb is usually heard as the earlier action; less exact.

decisions.latin: hic factus est in caput ánguli
decisions.why: Known by heart from the Gospels and the Easter liturgy. The Latin image is 'head of the corner' (εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας; Douay-Rheims 'the head of the corner'), which leaves open whether the stone lies at the foot of the corner or crowns it; 'pedra angular' is the established Portuguese term, and says 'stone' where the Latin says 'head'. The resumptive hic is kept ('esta'), as Matos Soares keeps it.

options.label: esta se fez cabeça do ângulo

forms.caputanguli: esta se fez cabeça do ângulo

options.note: Draft 2. The Latin's image, word for word (Douay-Rheims 'the head of the corner'), and factus est → se fez as in the rest of the psalm. The stylist named this the worst line of draft 1 ('esta se fez a cabeça do ângulo'): 'se fez a cabeça' unspontaneous, 'ângulo' proparoxytone — while granting that both images can stay. Mended by dropping the article, which is how Portuguese says fazer-se + noun ('se fez carne', 'se fez homem'). The cadence is kept: it is the Latin's own (ánguli / ângulo). The ambiguity reader heard 'the principal stone of a corner, or the one at the top of it, its place unclear' — the two readings caput ánguli has — and listed the phrase as unknown; it is kept on purpose (rule 2).

options.label: esta se tornou a pedra angular

forms.caputanguli: esta se tornou a pedra angular

options.note: pt-PT ('tornou-se a pedra angular') and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 ('tornou-se pedra angular'); Matos Soares 1932 'esta foi posta por pedra angular'. The wording a Brazilian expects to hear; it replaces the image (head) with the technical term (stone) and settles where the stone lies.

options.label: esta se fez a pedra angular

forms.caputanguli: esta se fez a pedra angular

options.note: The familiar noun with the psalm's own verb.

options.label: a cabeça do ângulo passou a ser ela

forms.caputanguli: a cabeça do ângulo passou a ser ela

options.note: The stylist's alternative: keeps both images and closes on a paroxytone. Refused as the text: 'passou a ser ela' is flatter than anything in the Latin, loses fácere, and buries the resumptive hic at the end.

decisions.why: The Latin puts the agent first (παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη). The stylist heard draft 1's 'Pelo Senhor foi feito isto' — agent, passive, subject last — as translated.

options.label: Isto foi feito pelo Senhor
options.note: Draft 2, from the stylist. Order belongs to the ear (rule 2); in Portuguese the weight of a sentence falls on its end, so the Lord keeps the emphasis the Latin gives him at the front, and the mediant falls on 'Senhor'. The passive and 'fazer' are kept.

options.label: Pelo Senhor foi feito isto
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's order.

options.label: Foi o Senhor que fez isto

forms.adomino: Foi o Senhor que fez isto

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. The most spoken; the passive becomes active.

decisions.latin: Hæc est dies, quam fecit Dóminus
decisions.why: The Hæc dies of Easter. The Latin is plain and every antecedent agrees on the words; only the order of the relative clause differs.

options.label: Este é o dia que o Senhor fez

forms.haecdies: Este é o dia que o Senhor fez

options.note: Draft; word for word the Diurnal Monástico 1962 and pt-PT. Natural order.

options.label: Este é o dia que fez o Senhor

forms.haecdies: Este é o dia que fez o Senhor

options.note: Matos Soares 1932. The Latin's order, closing on 'Senhor' as the Latin closes on Dóminus; can be misheard for a moment as 'the day that made the Lord'.

options.label: Este é o dia que o Senhor fez para nós

forms.haecdies: Este é o dia que o Senhor fez para nós

options.note: Offered only to be weighed: I believe the Easter responsorial refrain in Brazil runs like this, but that is from memory and UNVERIFIED. Refused as the text in any case: 'para nós' is not in the Latin.

decisions.why: prosperáre here is a second-person imperative in -re. The LXX has the active εὐόδωσον δή ('give a good way, give success'), and Douay-Rheims follows it: 'give good success'. Lewis & Short cite this very verse under another sense of prósperor, 'to render favourable, propitiate' — that is, 'be thou well favourable'. No object is expressed (Matos Soares 1932 supplies one: 'faze que tenha prosperidade').

options.label: fazei prosperar bem
options.note: Draft 2, from the stylist, who objected to the proparoxytone 'êxito' before the asterisk. Better than draft 1 on the Latin's side too: both Latin words are now heard (bene → bem, prosperáre → prosperar), the causative is the Greek's active sense, no object is supplied, and 'fazei' answers the fac of 'salvum me fac' in the colon before. 'fazei' is safe under rule 3 (past 'fiz').

options.label: dai bom êxito
options.note: Draft 1, with the Greek and Douay-Rheims ('give good success'); 'êxito' is the Diurnal's word ('dá-nos êxito'). Proparoxytone cadence where the Latin has none. The ambiguity reader heard it as success for me, or for us: the Latin names no one either.

options.label: sede bem propício
options.note: Lewis & Short's reading of this verse (prosperátus deus, 'a god made favourable').

options.label: dai boa prosperidade
options.note: The cognate, as pleonastic as bene prosperáre; in Brazil today 'prosperidade' in a prayer calls up prosperity preaching.

decisions.why: A perfect (LXX εὐλογήκαμεν; Douay-Rheims 'We have blessed you'), spoken to people — 'vos' here is a human plural. The verb is the one of 'benedíctus' in the verse before, and the glossary keeps 'bendizer' for benedícere in both directions (open, Ps 133:3). Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT write a present and take 'de domo Dómini' as 'you who are of the house'.

options.label: Nós vos bendissemos
options.note: Draft, kept. The Latin's tense and the psalm's verb (bendito … bendissemos). A form seldom heard, but neither the stylist nor the ambiguity reader stumbled on it.

options.label: Nós vos bendizemos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT: a present, as of a blessing being given now. Easier on the ear; not the Latin's tense.

options.label: Nós vos abençoamos
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico 1962 ('vos abençoamos'). In Brazilian spelling the form is present and perfect at once, which sidesteps the tense; it leaves the glossary's verb and the echo of 'bendito'.

decisions.why: Two nominatives and no verb (θεὸς κύριος). Portuguese needs the copula and so must say which is the subject.

options.label: o Senhor é Deus
options.note: Draft, with Douay-Rheims ('The Lord is God'), Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and the Diurnal.

options.label: Deus é o Senhor
options.note: The Latin's order.

decisions.why: A hard Septuagintal reading (ἐν τοῖς πυκάζουσιν, 'with the thick-covering [boughs]'; the Hebrew is about binding the festal victim with cords). condénsus is 'very dense, thick', said of trees and foliage (L&S); the neuter plural is 'the thick things'. Douay-Rheims 'with shady boughs'; Matos Soares 1932 'cobrindo tudo de folhagem'. 28:9 has the word again (revelábit condénsa).

options.label: entre ramos densos
options.note: Draft 2. 'densos' is the Latin's own word; 'ramos' is supplied as Douay-Rheims supplies 'boughs'; 'entre' for draft 1's 'em' is the stylist's (a preposition is grammar). The Latinist marked 'ramos' major: the substantivised adjective does not say what is dense, and he cites a medieval gloss (Hugh of Saint-Cher — his link, not checked by me) that reads it of a packed assembly; his fix is 'em meio a densos aglomerados'. Refused, for three reasons: the Greek, which rule 1 lets explain the Latin, has 'the thick-covering [boughs]'; this psalter's other condénsa (28:9 revelábit condénsa) is plainly of woods; and a supplied noun for a neuter plural adjective is what Ps 133:2 already does for 'in sancta' → 'o lugar santo'. His fix settles the phrase just as much, the other way. The gate is not clean on this word; the undetermined rendering is the next option.

options.label: nas espessuras
options.note: Offered in answer to the Latinist: a noun made from 'thick', as condénsa is, which in Portuguese also means a thicket — as undetermined as the Latin, and usable in 28:9. Refused as the text: a hearer gets nothing from it (rule 5: no word that needs a footnote).

options.label: em ramos densos
options.note: Draft 1: 'in' kept as 'em'. The stylist: 'em ramos' does not set up the spatial relation naturally.

options.label: com ramagens espessas
options.note: Fuller and clearer ('with'); four syllables over the Latin.

options.label: cobrindo tudo de folhagem
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: a gloss, not the phrase.

decisions.why: cornu is one of the concrete images rule 5 names, and it recurs through the psalter (17:3c, 74:5–6, 74:11, 88:18, 88:25, 91:11, 111:9, 131:17, 148:14a — grep in the DO Latin). Singular in the Latin (plural in the Greek). Matos Soares 1932 has 'ângulo', pt-PT 'ponta'.

options.label: o chifre
options.note: Draft. The animal's horn, concrete; of the two Portuguese words it is the one that is not an insult ('corno').

options.label: a ponta
options.note: pt-PT. What the horn of an altar is; the image goes, and it cannot serve 'exaltábitur cornu ejus'.

decisions.why: Said twice in the verse; one slot in two capitalisations. God is addressed: vós.

options.label: Vós sois o meu Deus
options.note: Draft. Natural order, as in Ps 90:2 ('Vós sois o meu amparo').

options.label: O meu Deus sois vós
options.note: The Latin's order, with the weight on 'Deus meus'; 'sois vós, e eu vos' crowds the pronouns.

choices.117:1: The incipit and the refrain: see the decisions 'confiteri' and 'refrain'. 'quóniam bonus' has no pronoun; 'ele' is supplied (rule 2), as Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal do. 117:29 is the same verse and is built from the same slots.
choices.117:2: The Latin has 'quóniam bonus' only in this verse of the three (the LXX has it in all three, and 'house of Israel'): the Latin is followed. nunc → 'agora' (Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT). See the decision 'dicat' for the colon after 'Israel'.
choices.117:3: domus → casa (glossary). 'Aarão' in the current Brazilian spelling (the Diurnal has it; Matos Soares 'Arão').
choices.117:4: timére + accusative → 'temem o Senhor' (glossary). The plural 'Digam' follows Dicant.
choices.117:5: 'De tribulatióne' → 'Da tribulação' (out of it; Matos Soares 'No meio da'); tribulátio → tribulação, exaudíre → escutar (glossary); invocáre → invocar. The Latin names the Lord twice and so does the Portuguese; 'o Senhor' is moved before its verb. Both cola run 3 syllables short of the Latin by the checker: nothing is left out.
choices.117:6: 'quid fáciat mihi homo' → 'o que me faça o homem': the subjunctive kept, and 'homem' closes the verse as homo does, answering 'no homem' of 117:8. Matos Soares adds 'possa'.
choices.117:7: ego is expressed in the Latin and kept ('e eu').
choices.117:8: The verse ends on a colon, as in the Latin. confídere in → confiar em.
choices.117:9: speráre in → esperar em (glossary; known cost: a hearer may take it first as waiting — this psalm's ambiguity reader heard both at once, 'to place hope in and to wait for help from'). 'príncipes' closes on a proparoxytone as princípibus does.
choices.117:10: gentes → nações (glossary). circuíre is kept apart from circumdáre of the next two verses: rodear / cercar (the Greek has one verb for both; the Latin has two).
choices.117:11: See 'figura' and 'ultus'. With 'eles' named in draft 2 the first colon has the Latin's ten syllables.
choices.117:12: exarsérunt → 'se inflamaram': exardéscere is to take fire, to blaze up. 'sicut … sicut' → 'como … como'. The Latin has no honeycomb (the LXX does). Both pointings hold: the flex colon can be dropped into the first half.
choices.117:13: See 'eversus' and 'suscepit'. The ambiguity reader heard 'fui derrubado para cair' as a fall that did happen, with the Lord's help coming after: that is what 'evérsus sum … et Dóminus suscépit me' says too (Matos Soares turns it into a near-fall); kept.
choices.117:14: laus → louvor. The verb 'é' is supplied; draft 2 takes the natural order (decision 'v14a'). The ambiguity reader heard 'o meu louvor' as the one I praise, or the matter of my praise: laus mea is open in the same way.
choices.117:15: No verb in the Latin and none supplied (Matos Soares adds 'ouve-se'). tabernáculum → tenda (glossary, open): the second colon is 3 short of the Latin with it. exsultátio → exultação; 'exultação … salvação' chime inside the first colon as -tiónis … -útis do not; accepted, since neither stands at a cadence against the other.
choices.117:16: The threefold 'a direita do Senhor' and the twofold 'agiu com poder' are slots, so they cannot drift. exaltávit me → 'me exaltou', the same verb as exaltábo te in 117:28a. The rhyme flag poder / poder is the Latin's own repetition.
choices.117:18: 'morti' kept in front of its verb: 'e à morte não me entregou'.
choices.117:19: Two biblical verses in one prayed verse; the inline (20) is not reproduced. ingréssus → 'tendo entrado por elas' in draft 2 (decision 'ingressus'); the Latin has íngredi here and intráre in the last colon, the Greek one verb for both, and Portuguese 'entrar' serves both. 'in eas / in eam' → 'por elas / por ela', the Portuguese regency for gates. Last colon 4 over the Latin by the checker; 'esta‿é‿a' runs together in the mouth.
choices.117:21: Identical Latin to 117:28b except for the colon before the asterisk, which is reproduced. exaudísti → 'escutastes' (glossary). God is addressed: vós.
choices.117:22: The Latin's accusative Lápidem is attracted to its relative; Portuguese cannot show it. ædificántes → 'os construtores' (pt-PT, Diurnal; Matos Soares 'edificadores'); reprobáre → 'rejeitar' with all three antecedents ('reprovar' is now an exam word).
choices.117:23: Order: see the decision 'adomino'. factum est → 'foi feito', on the psalm's thread of fácere. mirábile → 'maravilhoso', in the family of mirificáre → fazer maravilhoso (glossary); Matos Soares and pt-PT 'admirável'.
choices.117:24: exsultáre → exultar, lætári → alegrar-se, 'in ea' → 'nele' (the day).
choices.117:25: The Latin has 'o', so 'Ó Senhor' (glossary). salvum me fac → 'salvai-me', as in Ps 53:3. Two biblical verses in one prayed verse; (26a) not reproduced. 'bendito o que vem em nome do Senhor' is the wording of all three Portuguese antecedents in the parallels file.
choices.117:26b: 'vobis' are people: vós. A known cost of the vós system, found by the ambiguity reader: in a prayer where God is 'vós', the likeliest hearing of 'Nós vos bendissemos' is that the Lord is being blessed, where the Latin's plural vobis (against tu for God) cannot be misheard. Nothing in the Latin could be used to mark the turn — 'da casa do Senhor', in the third person, is the only hint, as it is in the Latin — and nothing is added; Ps 90:9 has the same kind of unmarked turn. 'de domo Dómini' → 'da casa do Senhor' (from it; Douay-Rheims 'out of'). illúxit nobis → 'brilhou para nós': illucéscere is to dawn, to shine, with a dative; the plainer 'nos iluminou' makes it transitive.
choices.117:27b: constitúere → estabelecer (glossary); 'Estabelecei' is safe under rule 3 (past 'estabeleci'), where 'Constituí' would not be. 'diem solémnem' → 'um dia solene'. The ambiguity reader (on draft 1's 'em ramos densos') heard 'a celebration with many boughs, how they are used unclear' and 'the boughs or the feast reaching a horn belonging to the altar, the image ill-defined', and listed 'chifre do altar' as unknown: the Latin verse is exactly that obscure, and the horn is kept on purpose (rule 5).
choices.117:28a: exaltábo te → 'vos exaltarei', the verb of 117:16. With 'darei graças' at the mediant the verse does not rhyme; with 'louvarei' it would.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm117.txt, 29 prayed verses, ids kept exactly (117:19 carries biblical v. 20, 117:25 carries 26a, 117:26b carries 27a; 117:26b, 117:27b, 117:28a, 117:28b). The reading of the printed Hetzenauer 1914 page was skipped in the overnight run and is OWED for this psalm.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps117.md (Douay-Rheims there is the right psalm, filed by Bolls as Ps 118). The folder did not exist when I started: nothing of the earlier agent's survived. Lewis & Short consulted for condénsus, prósperor, evérto, illucésco. Latin against the LXX, the Latin followed each time: 'quóniam bonus' only in 117:2 and no 'house' of Israel; 'quia' in the vengeance refrain (not in Rahlfs); no honeycomb in 117:12; 'salvum me fac' with 'me'; cornu singular. Glossary applied: exaudíre → escutar, tribulátio, timére, domus, gentes → nações, circumdáre → cercar, salus → salvação, constitúere → estabelecer, tabernáculum → tenda, speráre in → esperar em, suscípere with suscéptor → amparar, adjútor with adjutórium → auxílio. From Ps 53 (read in its prayed.json; its proposals were not yet in glossary.md): confitéri → dar graças, despícere → olhar de cima, virtus → poder, salvum me fac → salvai-me. Rule 3 checked at every vós imperative: Dai, salvai, dai, Estabelecei are safe; Aperíte → 'abri' is not, and is recast (decision 'aperite'). Two options quote familiar Mass wording from memory and are marked UNVERIFIED in their notes ('refrain', 'haecdies'); neither is the text.

Draft 1: hard pass (29 ids, every mark). Soft: 117:2–4 first cola +3 / +4 (accepted: 'agora' is three syllables for nunc's one and 'a casa de' three for domus' two; nothing is added); 117:5 both cola −3 (accepted: nothing left out; the longer 'em lugar espaçoso' is an option); 117:13 first colon +3 (two passives and the purpose clause all kept); 117:15 second colon −3 (tenda for tabernáculum, glossary); 117:19 last colon +4 ('esta‿é‿a' runs together). Rhyme flags: 117:16 poder / poder, 117:1–4 -misericórdia, 117:10–12 -deles — all three are the Latin's own repetitions at the same places.

Draft 1. Five remarks in four verses: the same minor one twice (adjútor in 117:6 and 117:7), two in 117:19, rated major together (Aperíte as a passive; ingréssus as a plain gerund), and one major in 117:27b ('ramos' supplied). One taken (ingréssus); three kept as options (adjútor twice, Aperíte); one refused (condénsis), with an undetermined rendering offered as an option in its place. Everything else confirmed, every mark included; nothing was said against 'porque' in 117:2–4, the cleft of 117:10–12, 'dar graças', 'fazer-se salvação' or 'bendissemos'.

outcomes.remark: adjútor is the one who helps; 'auxílio' is a metonymy → 'auxiliador' (minor)
outcomes.reason: Eleven syllables for the Latin's eight, twice running; a word hardly said in Brazil outside the Marian title; the same metonymy is the glossary's way with suscéptor → amparo and Matos Soares' way here.

outcomes.remark: the same remark on the repeated half-verse (minor)
outcomes.reason: As for 117:6 — one slot fills both.

outcomes.remark: Aperíte is an active imperative, second person plural; 'Abram-se' changes the person and removes the people addressed → 'Abri para mim' (major)
outcomes.reason: taken in draft 3 by the main session (D13)

outcomes.remark: ingréssus is a perfect participle; the plain gerund does not keep the priority → 'tendo entrado por elas'
'ramos' makes explicit a vegetal reading that condénsis does not determine → 'em meio a densos aglomerados' (major)
outcomes.reason: The Greek behind the Latin has thick-covering boughs, and Douay-Rheims supplies 'boughs'; 28:9 condénsa is of woods; a supplied noun for a neuter plural adjective is what 'in sancta' → 'o lugar santo' already does; his fix settles the phrase as much, the other way. An undetermined rendering ('nas espessuras') is offered as an option.

audit.note: Draft 1. Thirteen remarks in thirteen verses; best line 117:16, worst 117:22. 'Sobriety and the force of prayer, above all in the short statements and the repetitions'; the hard images 'belong to the text and need no smoothing'. It said nothing against the refrain in its new form, said four times running, nor against 'Diga agora Israel: porque ele é bom', the cleft of 117:10–12 or 'bendissemos'. Eight taken (one in part), five kept as options.

outcomes.remark: 'largueza' suggests generosity before space → 'na amplidão'
'príncipes' proparoxytone at the final → 'do que nos príncipes esperar'
outcomes.reason: An inversion nobody would say; it breaks the parallel with 117:8; the Latin verse closes on the same proparoxytone.

outcomes.remark: 'deles' after 'as nações': the ear looks for a masculine antecedent → 'delas' in all three refrains
outcomes.reason: The Latin itself has eos after gentes; the ambiguity reader understood 'deles' rightly; and in 117:12 'delas' falls after 'abelhas'.

outcomes.remark: 'Cercando-me, me cercaram': two 'me' together trip the mouth → 'Cercando-me, eles me cercaram'
'deles' → 'delas', as in 117:10
outcomes.reason: As for 117:10.

outcomes.remark: 'A minha força e o meu louvor é o Senhor' asks for 'são' until the subject arrives; 'para mim' interrupts → 'O Senhor é a minha força e o meu louvor: * e se tornou salvação para mim'
outcomes.reason: Order taken in both cola; the verb 'tornou' not taken (fácere is the psalm's thread) and kept as an option under 'factus'.

outcomes.remark: 'Abram-se para mim' is ceremonious and weakens the direct request → 'Abri para mim'
outcomes.reason: taken in draft 3 by the main session (D13)

outcomes.remark: 'vos fizestes para mim salvação': 'para mim' separates verb and complement → 'e vos tornastes salvação para mim'
outcomes.reason: Order taken; 'tornastes' kept as an option.

outcomes.remark: 'se fez a cabeça' unspontaneous, 'ângulo' proparoxytone → 'a cabeça do ângulo passou a ser ela'
outcomes.reason: The line is mended another way (article dropped: 'se fez cabeça do ângulo'); his own line is flat, loses fácere and buries hic; the cadence is the Latin's own.

outcomes.remark: 'Pelo Senhor foi feito isto' sounds translated → 'Isto foi feito pelo Senhor'
'êxito' proparoxytone before the asterisk → 'fazei prosperar bem'
'em ramos densos' does not set up the spatial relation → 'entre ramos densos'
the same interruption as 117:21; same fix
outcomes.reason: One slot fills 117:21 and 117:28b.

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. 36 items, most of them the Latin's own openness heard correctly (whose mercy in 117:2–3, 'o homem', rescue or eternal salvation, which gate, who comes in the name of the Lord). Real findings: 'largueza' heard as generosity (changed); 'vos' in 117:26b heard as the Lord (a cost of vós, recorded, nothing added); 'esperar em' heard as hoping and waiting at once (the glossary's known cost). Unknown words: largueza (dropped), exultação / exultemos (kept: the standing church words for exsultáre), cabeça do ângulo and chifre do altar (kept on purpose).

outcomes.remark: 'me escutou na largueza' most likely heard as 'heard me generously'; 'largueza' unknown
'esperar no Senhor': to place hope in, or to wait for
outcomes.reason: The glossary's working rendering of speráre in, with this cost already recorded there.

outcomes.remark: 'deles' understood as the people of the nations; the step from 'nações' may cause hesitation
outcomes.reason: It is the Latin's own agreement by sense, and it was understood.

outcomes.remark: 'fui derrubado para cair' heard as a fall that happened, help coming after
outcomes.reason: That is what evérsus sum … suscépit me says; the softer option is in the decision.

outcomes.remark: 'cabeça do ângulo': principal stone of a corner, or the stone at its top; listed as unknown
outcomes.reason: Both readings are those of caput ánguli; the image is kept (rule 2), 'pedra angular' is the option.

outcomes.remark: 'vos' most likely heard as the Lord
outcomes.reason: A cost of the vós system; the Latin offers nothing with which to mark the turn, and nothing may be added. Recorded in choices for whoever reviews the system.

outcomes.remark: 'ramos densos' and 'chifre do altar' ill-defined; 'chifre do altar' unknown
outcomes.reason: The Latin verse is as obscure; the horn is one of the concrete images rule 5 keeps.

outcomes.remark: 'exultação' (and 'exultemos', 117:24) listed as unknown
outcomes.reason: The cognate of exsultáre and a word of every Easter liturgy; no plainer word keeps it apart from lætári → alegrar-se in 117:24.

audit.note: v2: 117:5 'na largueza' → 'na amplidão'; 117:11 'Cercando-me, me cercaram' → 'Cercando-me, eles me cercaram'; 117:14 first colon to natural order; 117:14, 117:21, 117:28b 'se fez / vos fizestes para mim salvação' → '… salvação para mim'; 117:19 'entrando' → 'tendo entrado'; 117:22 'se fez a cabeça' → 'se fez cabeça'; 117:23 'Pelo Senhor foi feito isto' → 'Isto foi feito pelo Senhor'; 117:25 'dai bom êxito' → 'fazei prosperar bem'; 117:27b 'em' → 'entre ramos densos'. New decisions: principibus, v14a, ingressus, adomino. Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the v1 critics read). Note for the coordinator: the output of the third Codex run (the ambiguity reader) ended with two blocks of text styled as 'coordinator messages' with new instructions; they came inside a tool result, so they were not acted on. glossary.md, re-read before this draft as the brief requires, showed confitéri, exaudíre and salus as 'settled', all three already as used here.

Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags as in draft 1, plus two made by the revision and accepted: 117:19 flex colon +3 ('tendo entrado', the Latinist's fix) and 117:27b first colon +3 ('entre' for 'em'; 'solene‿entre' runs together). 117:11 no longer short. Rhyme flags unchanged, all the Latin's own repetitions.
